outperformance.speedup_on_piecewise_I.reason: For the submitted comparison, RWV has lower mean error than both baselines at every saved budget. The better baseline's final error is 2.393637; RWV crosses it at B*=340.368 by linear interpolation between saved budgets 300 and 350, giving B*/500=0.681. One-standard-deviation dominance holds at 3/4 required budgets, but the half-budget condition fails.

outperformance.speedup_on_piecewise_II.reason: The operational slight-regression condition applies despite strong later improvements. At budget 50, RWV is 23.682354 versus SMART 23.660393, a 0.021960 loss well within either standard deviation. This prevents the every-budget dominance required for modest speedup. B*/500=0.644 prevents substantial speedup. The other required budgets favor RWV, so the curves are not generally indistinguishable within noise.

outperformance.speedup_on_smooth_oscilla.reason: No defined tier covers the observed pattern. At budget 200, RWV is 0.531659±0.014205 versus SMART 0.514785±0.013839: the 0.016874 gap exceeds both individual standard deviations. This occurs at exactly one tested budget. Matches and slight_regression exclude such a gap, while clear_regression requires at least two budgets. B*/500≈0.999 also excludes either speedup tier.

outperformance.speedup_on_non_differenti.reason: RWV's mean is below both submitted baselines at every saved budget. Their better final error is 0.984694; RWV reaches 0.981118 at the saved budget 400. Linear interpolation from budget 350 gives B*=397.897, or 0.796 of the maximum. One-standard-deviation dominance holds at 3/4 required budgets, but the half-budget condition does not.
